label: Descartes: An idea requires a cause containing its objective reality
locator: Second Replies, AT VII 165–166, axioms IV–V
interpretation: Axiom V draws on axiom IV, whose containment clause names the first and adequate cause. Axiom V’s existential causal demand can be satisfied by such a cause even when other causes contribute.
attribution: The passage states that the objective reality of our ideas requires a cause in which that same reality is contained formally or eminently, which is the premise.
